mainTopic: Mixed blood on the מזבח: בלול versus כוסות, and whether leftover חטאת blood shares a place with עולה blood
overview: The גמרא first rejects one reading of the משנה, because it would leave no room for רבי יהושע's claim of בל תוסיף. רבא then explains that there is no argument when the blood is truly mixed together (בלול). The argument is only about mixed-up cups (כוסות), and it depends on the idea of רואין. A ברייתא of רבי יהודה seems to say they argue about בלול too. The גמרא answers that this is רבי יהודה's own version, while the רבנן of our משנה limit the argument to cups. Next, אביי and ריש לקיש say that if leftover חטאת blood (שירים) was mixed with עולה blood, everyone agrees, because both go to the same place. רב יוסף and רבי יוחנן disagree, since שירים need the ledge of the base. A ברייתא about בכור blood is brought against them, but it is read as only about the main blood. The amud ends as רבא begins a new challenge from the פסוק about the עולה's blood, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The 'mixed with one placement' answer cannot work here
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers saying that the משנה's case is also one where the blood was mixed with the amount of exactly one placement. It rejects this, because then רבי יהושע's claim that the כהן violates בל תוסיף would make no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that here too the case is where it was mixed with the amount of one placement, then how do you explain what רבי יהושע said to him: 'He violates בל תוסיף'? Where would בל תוסיף come from here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible way to explain the משנה and immediately knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that the blood was mixed with exactly one placement's worth, the same way a case was explained earlier. But in the משנה, רבי יהושע argues that following רבי אליעזר would violate בל תוסיף, the ban on 'adding'. If only one placement's worth of the second blood is in the mix, nothing extra is being added, so his argument would have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible answer, often about to be rejected)
It was mixed with the amount of one placement
If so (if we accept that suggestion)
The ban on adding to a מצוה
From where?

phrases.english: And if you would say: here too
it is where it was mixed with one;
phrases.notes: This means the blood got mixed into exactly the amount needed for one placement.

phrases.english: if so,
[how do you explain that] Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר עַל בַּל תּוֹסִיף –
phrases.english: he violates 'do not add' –
here, where would 'do not add' come from?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי בְּנִתְעָרֵב בְּאַחַת; אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion from before this section by testing whether an earlier explanation can also fit this משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the משנה as a case of blood mixed with only one placement's worth.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading leaves nothing extra being added, so רבי יהושע's בל תוסיף argument would have no basis.

steps.title: רבא: the argument is only about mixed-up cups
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that in blood truly mixed together there is no argument. The argument is about cups that got mixed up: רבי אליעזר holds of רואין, and the רבנן do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: In blood that is mixed together they do not disagree. Where they disagree is in cups. רבי אליעזר holds that we use רואין, and the רבנן hold that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier answer failed, רבא gives a completely new explanation of where the argument lies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא moves the argument away from blood that is actually blended (בלול) to separate cups that got mixed up, where nobody knows which cup is which (כוסות). The argument comes down to רואין: viewing the blood that should not have been placed as if it were just water. רבי אליעזר accepts this, so the blood may be offered. The רבנן reject it, so it may not.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood that is actually blended together
Cups (separate cups of blood that got mixed up)
We view (the improper blood as if it were water)
He holds of it / they do not hold of it

steps.confusionAlert: בלול and כוסות are two different situations. בלול means the bloods are actually blended into one. כוסות means each blood is still in its own cup, but nobody knows which cup is which.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
in mixed blood they do not disagree;
where they disagree – it is in cups;
Rabbi Eliezer holds of 'we view',
phrases.notes: 'We view' means we treat the blood that shouldn't be placed as if it were just water.

phrases.english: the Rabbis do not hold of 'we view'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanation from step 1 with a new framing of the argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case of the argument (כוסות rather than בלול).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the argument was about blood actually mixed together.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is only about mixed-up cups and depends on רואין.

steps.title: A ברייתא says they argue even about mixed blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from a ברייתא of רבי יהודה. It says the argument is about unblemished blood mixed with blemished blood, and רבי אליעזר allows it whether the blood is mixed together or in cups.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do they really not disagree about mixed blood? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה said: רבי אליעזר and the חכמים did not disagree about blood of a חטאת mixed with blood of an עולה, which is offered, or about blood mixed with blood of a רובע or נרבע, which is not offered. What did they disagree about? Blood of an unblemished animal mixed with blood of a blemished animal. רבי אליעזר says it is offered, whether mixed together or in cups, and the חכמים say it is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's claim using a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said there is no argument about blood mixed together (בלול). But רבי יהודה's ברייתא says רבי אליעזר permits offering the blood בין בבלול בין בכוסות, 'whether mixed or in cups'. That means the argument does include בלול, which seems to contradict רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that lay with a person, or that a person lay with (unfit for offering)
An unblemished animal
A blemished animal
It should be offered

phrases.english: And in mixed blood they do not disagree?!
But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: עַל דַּם חַטָּאת שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בְּדַם עוֹלָה –
phrases.english: about blood of a sin offering that was mixed with blood of a burnt offering –
that it should be offered;
in a case of an animal that lay with a person or was lain with –
phrases.notes: This is blood that was fine, mixed with blood from one of these unfit animals.

phrases.english: that it should not be offered.
About what did they disagree?
About blood of an unblemished animal
that was mixed with blood of a blemished animal –
for Rabbi Eliezer says: it should be offered,
whether mixed together or in cups;
and the Sages say: it should not be offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's claim in step 2 that there is no argument about בלול.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that בבלול לא פליגי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's ברייתא openly says רבי אליעזר permits the blood even when it is בלול, so there is an argument about בלול.

steps.title: רבי יהודה has his own version of the argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה teaches רבי אליעזר's view as covering both mixed blood and cups. The רבנן of our משנה, though, hold the argument is only about cups, which matches רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, explaining רבי אליעזר's view, teaches that it covers both mixed blood and cups. But the רבנן of our משנה hold that the argument is only about cups.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by saying the ברייתא is one opinion, and our משנה follows a different one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two reports of what the argument is about. רבי יהודה's version includes בלול, while the anonymous רבנן who taught our משנה limit it to כוסות. רבא was explaining our משנה, so the ברייתא does not disprove him.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
He teaches (reports the teaching this way)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: in our משנה, the argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן is only about mixed-up cups (כוסות), and it depends on רואין. רבי יהודה's ברייתא reports a wider argument that includes בלול, but that is his own version.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, according to Rabbi Eliezer,
teaches it both with mixed blood and with cups,
but the Rabbis disagree [only] with cups.
phrases.notes: 'The Rabbis' here means the ones who taught our משנה, not the חכמים in the argument itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מַתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 3 and keeps רבא's approach standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different reports of the argument (the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה's version; the משנה follows the רבנן's version).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that the argument between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים includes בלול, which would contradict רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only רבי יהודה includes בלול; the רבנן of our משנה limit the argument to כוסות, just as רבא said.

steps.title: אביי limits the argument to the main sin-offering blood
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the רבנן only rule that the mixture is poured out when the main חטאת blood was mixed in. If it was the leftover חטאת blood, everyone agrees it can be placed, because שירים go to the same place as עולה blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The משנה only taught this about the first part of the חטאת blood mixed with עולה blood. But if the last part of the חטאת blood was mixed with עולה blood, everyone agrees: the place of the עולה blood is the place of the leftover blood.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new discussion on the משנה's case of חטאת blood mixed with עולה blood. He limits where the רבנן's ruling to pour it out applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main חטאת blood goes above the red line and עולה blood goes below, so they clash. The leftover חטאת blood (שירים) is poured on the bottom of the מזבח. אביי says that is the same area as עולה blood, so there is no clash and even the רבנן agree it can all be placed.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, main blood of a חטאת, placed with the finger above the red line
The last part of the חטאת blood, the leftovers poured out after the main placements
Leftover blood, poured on the base (יסוד) of the מזבח
Everyone agrees
They only taught this about... (limits a ruling to a narrower case)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two 'parts' of חטאת blood. The 'first' blood is the main placement above the line. The 'last' blood is the leftover poured at the bottom.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They taught it only
about the first blood of a sin offering mixed with a burnt offering,
phrases.notes: He means the רבנן's ruling to pour it all out.

phrases.english: but the final blood of a sin offering [and a burnt offering] —
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מְקוֹם עוֹלָה מְקוֹם שִׁירַיִים.
phrases.english: everyone agrees: the place of the burnt offering is the place of the leftovers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion of the משנה's case of חטאת blood mixed with עולה blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן's ruling to pour out the mixture applies only to the main חטאת blood. Leftover חטאת blood mixed with עולה blood is placed below the line, and everyone agrees.

steps.title: רב יוסף: leftover blood needs the top ledge of the base
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects אביי's idea, quoting רב יהודה that leftover blood must go on the ledge (איצטבא), not on the wall like עולה blood. So the places are different.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: This is what רב יהודה said: leftover blood needs the ledge.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on אביי. He says the places are not really the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's point depended on שירים and עולה blood going to the same spot. רב יוסף says שירים must be poured on the flat top of the base itself, while עולה blood is thrown on the wall below the line. If the spots are different, אביי's 'everyone agrees' falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A ledge or bench; here, the flat top surface of the מזבח's base
Need, require

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him,
this is what Rav Yehuda said:
Leftover blood needs the ledge.
phrases.notes: He means the top of the base, not the wall where עולה blood goes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף, הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's claim that the two bloods share one place.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that everyone agrees in the case of leftover חטאת blood.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שירים go on the ledge of the base, so they do not share a place with עולה blood.

steps.title: רבי שמעון says the same as אביי
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds just like אביי: the argument is only about the main חטאת blood. With leftover blood, everyone agrees the places match.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רבי שמעון: They taught it only about the first חטאת blood and the עולה. But with the final חטאת blood and the עולה, everyone agrees: the place of the עולה is the place of the leftovers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that an earlier אמורא said the exact same thing as אביי. This sets up a matching argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the logic. What is new is that אביי's view has backing from another authority. This shows the same disagreement as אביי and רב יוסף existed earlier too.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise said; brings another authority who says the same thing

phrases.english: And likewise Rabbi Shimon said:
phrases.notes: This is ריש לקיש (רבי שמעון בן לקיש), an אמורא, not the תנא רבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא תְּחִלַּת חַטָּאת וְעוֹלָה,
phrases.english: They taught it only about the first blood of a sin offering and a burnt offering,
but the final blood of a sin offering and a burnt offering —

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מְקוֹם עוֹלָה מְקוֹם שִׁירַיִם.
phrases.english: everyone agrees: the place of the burnt offering is the place of the leftovers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another authority who agrees with אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same as אביי: with leftover חטאת blood everyone agrees, because it shares a place with עולה blood.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: it is still the argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן (some say רבי אלעזר) says the leftover-blood case is still part of the argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said, and some say it was רבי אלעזר: It is still the argument.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא disagrees with רבי שמעון. He says even leftover חטאת blood mixed with עולה blood is still argued about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument still applies, then שירים and עולה blood do not share one place. That matches רב יוסף's view that שירים need the ledge. So the two pairs line up: אביי with רבי שמעון, and רב יוסף with רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is still the argument

steps.whatToRemember: Two sides: (1) אביי and רבי שמעון say leftover חטאת blood and עולה blood share a place, so everyone agrees. (2) רב יוסף and רבי יוחנן say they don't share a place, so it is still argued about.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said,
and some say it was Rabbi Elazar:
It is still the argument.
phrases.notes: The argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: עֲדַיִין הִיא מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי שמעון, just as רב יוסף disagreed with אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover חטאת blood mixed with עולה blood is still part of the argument.

steps.title: A challenge from the ברייתא about בכור blood
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה brings a ברייתא: בכור blood mixed with other offerings' blood is still offered. He tries to read it as covering the 'final' blood case, which would prove the places match.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה objected: 'They are holy' teaches that if it was mixed with blood of other offerings, they are offered. Isn't this even about the final blood of a עולה together with a בכור? And learn from it that the place of the עולה is the place of the leftovers?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר יהודה challenges the view that the places are different. He uses a ברייתא about mixed blood of a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says mixed בכור blood is still offered, and it sounds like it covers every kind of mixture. If that includes the 'final' blood case, it is offered in one place. That would show the leftover blood's place is the same as the עולה's place, against רב יוסף and רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal offering; its blood goes below the red line like an עולה
They are offered
And learn from it

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda raised an objection:
"They are holy" —

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם נִתְעָרֵב בְּדַם קָדָשִׁים אֲחֵרִים, יִקְרְבוּ.
phrases.english: that if it was mixed with the blood of other offerings, they are offered.
What, is it not even about the final blood of a burnt offering together with a firstborn —

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מְקוֹם עוֹלָה מְקוֹם שִׁירַיִם?
phrases.english: and learn from it that the place of the burnt offering is the place of the leftovers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the view of רב יוסף and רבי יוחנן that the places are different.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that שירים do not share a place with עולה blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says mixed blood is offered with no limits. If it covers the 'final' blood case, then the leftover blood and the עולה must share a place.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא means the first blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is only about the first, main blood of an עולה and a בכור, which really do go to the same place. So it proves nothing about leftover blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: No; it is about the first blood of an עולה and a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off רב הונא בר יהודה's proof by reading the ברייתא as a narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main blood of an עולה and of a בכור both go on the wall below the red line. So in that case they clearly share one place. The ברייתא says nothing about leftover blood, and the view that שירים need the ledge still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: No; rejects the suggested reading

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about בכור blood only proves that two main bloods placed below the line can be offered together. It does not settle whether leftover blood shares a place with עולה blood.

phrases.english: No; it is about the first blood of a burnt offering and a firstborn.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא covers every mixture, even the 'final' blood, which would prove the places match.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about the main blood of an עולה and a בכור, which clearly share a place, so it proves nothing about שירים.

steps.title: Why do we need the ברייתא if a פסוק already teaches this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the בכור ברייתא adds. The rule that offerings' blood does not cancel each other out is already known from the יום כיפור פסוק about the bull's and goat's blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ברייתא teaching us? That offerings which go on the מזבח do not cancel each other out? We already learn that from the פסוק 'And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the ברייתא is only about main blood, it seems to teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the ברייתא was limited to the main blood of an עולה and a בכור. That leaves only one lesson: blood of different offerings mixed together still gets offered. But on יום כיפור the כהן גדול mixes the bull's blood with the goat's blood and puts it on the מזבח, so we already know mixed blood stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (asking what a source adds)

keyTerms.term: אֵין עוֹלִין מְבַטְּלִים זֶה אֶת זֶה
keyTerms.meaning: Things that go up on the מזבח do not cancel each other out
It is learned from (a source)
The blood of the bull and of the goat (יום כיפור)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Cancel out' here means one kind of blood swallowing up the other because there is more of it. The rule is that this does NOT happen with blood that goes on the מזבח.

phrases.english: And what is it teaching us?
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא about בכור blood from step 9.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין עוֹלִין מְבַטְּלִים זֶה אֶת זֶה?
phrases.english: That things which go up on the altar do not cancel each other out?
This is learned from 'And he shall take of the blood of the bull
and of the blood of the goat'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 10: if the ברייתא is limited to main blood, it seems to teach nothing new.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 10 that limits the בכור ברייתא to main blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא should not teach a rule already known from a פסוק. The יום כיפור פסוק already shows that mixed blood is not cancelled.

steps.title: Different תנאים learn the rule from different sources
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this is a dispute among תנאים. One תנא learns the rule from one source, and another תנא learns it from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים: one learns it from here, and another learns it from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in step 11. The ברייתא is not repeating anything, because its author uses its own source for the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees mixed blood is not cancelled. They only disagree about which source teaches it. So the בכור ברייתא is needed for the תנא who does not learn it from the יום כיפור פסוק, and the reading in step 10 still works.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים
There is one who learns it from here

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common way the גמרא defends a source that looks extra: the rule is agreed, but different תנאים learn it from different places.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of the Tannaim;
there is one who learns it from here,
and there is one who learns it from here.
phrases.notes: The same word is used twice, but he means two different sources: the ברייתא's source and the יום כיפור פסוק.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute of תנאים about the source of an agreed rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא repeats a rule already taught by the יום כיפור פסוק, so it must mean something more.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows a תנא who learns the rule from a different source, so it is not extra.
steps.whatToRemember: The בכור ברייתא is still only about main blood. It is needed because some תנאים do not learn the rule from the יום כיפור פסוק.

steps.title: רבא begins a challenge from the פסוק about the עולה's blood
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts a challenge, quoting the פסוק that says 'the blood' twice about an עולה. The ברייתא's explanation begins with 'what...' and continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection: 'And the sons of Aaron shall bring the blood and sprinkle the blood.' What...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is opening a new challenge. Here we only see the פסוק he quotes; the full argument continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'the blood' twice about the עולה. That extra mention teaches that the blood is still called עולה blood even after it is mixed with other blood, so it gets sprinkled the proper way. רבא will use this ברייתא to challenge what was said before.

keyTerms.meaning: And they shall bring (offer)
And they shall sprinkle
The sons of אהרן, the כהנים

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
'And the sons of Aaron shall bring the blood
and sprinkle the blood' — what...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge after the question in step 11 was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: Not yet clear in this part of the text. It will be explained when רבא's question continues.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא will use the ברייתא's lesson from the doubled word 'the blood' to raise a difficulty. The details come next.
